span: this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
proposal: A relation between an official traffic-control device and the intersection it controls - equivalently, a region kind for the approach of an intersection together with its connection to that intersection region - so that "intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices" can be read of the very junction the two vehicles entered. The vocabulary relates a device only to the traffic it faces (dev.governs: a lane, approach or region), and relates regions to one another only lane-to-lane (st.lane_connectivity); no atom ties the region a device governs to an intersection region, no atom gives a distance from a device to a region (st.region_geometry measures only from a road user's body outline, dev.position carries a location alone) and no primitive of SS10 computes one. Every reading the vocabulary allows therefore does one of two excluded things. Either it names the intersection region itself as the governed region, which dev.governs' contract excludes outright. Or it substitutes for the approach a region that runs the whole length of the way - st.highway, "the entire public way between its boundary lines", or st.lane, "a longitudinal strip of roadway", both of which continue through every junction of that way - so that a stop sign or signal at any other junction the subject's way passes through exempts this one, which is the approximation the review returned; and st.lane fails a second time, because inside the crossing, where the trigger puts both vehicles, the subject occupies no lane, so the exception would be false exactly when the rule applies and the span would be silently dropped. The span cannot be assumed either: SS9's clause "Where the same category is also marked on the road by a sign (dev.zone_sign), the sign is the atom and the category is not" governs this category, since the control of an intersection is marked on the road by the very devices SS4 carries as atoms - what is missing is not the category but the relation that attaches those devices to this junction. s6 is an exception span, which rule 3 forbids dropping or narrowing, so the node is withdrawn for the operator to decide the gap.
nearest: dev.governs: "relation: the device applies to a lane, approach or region (which traffic it faces) - Not a stand-in for: a position - the region a device acts on is not where a halt is required and not the intersection region" - the closing words exclude naming the intersection the pair entered as the region the device governs, which is what "intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices" asserts.

st.highway: "the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders" - a region that runs the whole length of the way and through every junction on it, so a device governing it is not a device controlling this intersection.

st.lane: "a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles - Not a stand-in for: a half of the roadway or a lateral position within a lane" - a lane likewise continues past the junction, and a vehicle inside the crossing, where this rule reads, is on no lane.
st.lane_connectivity: "which lane a lane leads into" - relates one lane to another lane and never a lane or an approach to an intersection region.

dev.position: "location of the device head / sign face - Not a stand-in for: a stop line or a crossing - the distance to a signal head is a different quantity from the distance to the line or region" - a device's location with no relation to, and no distance to, the intersection region.

st.region_geometry: "the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame, and the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it" - the distance it carries is from a road user, never from a device, and it relates no two regions.

span: upon the approach to or near the crest of a grade,
proposal: | `st.crest` | the point of a roadway at which its longitudinal slope changes from rising to falling in the direction of travel, carried as a region of the road structure with a reference point and a boundary, so that the ground distance from a road user to it is read through `st.region_geometry`; false on a roadway whose profile has no such sign change, and absent on a source that maps no vertical profile **Not a stand-in for:** the slope at a point (`st.grade`), the view a crest restricts (`st.sight_distance`), or a horizontal bend (`st.curvature`) | general |
nearest: st.grade - 'longitudinal slope of the roadway; a crest is its sign change': the contract names the crest but carries only the slope at the point observed, so a read at the road user's own position yields neither the crest's location nor the distance to it, and no primitive of section 10 evaluates an atom at a point offset ahead along the roadway, so 'the approach to or near the crest' cannot be formed from it.

st.sight_distance - 'distance along the road within which another vehicle would be visible from a point': this is what a crest restricts, not where the crest is; reading it for the crest substitutes the consequence for the feature, and it would collide with this same sentence's separate visibility condition, which states its own distance of 500 feet.

st.region_geometry - 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame, and the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it': it supplies exactly the distance this span needs, but only for a structure region the ontology defines, and no region of section 3 denotes a crest.

st.curvature - 'horizontal curvature of the roadway at a point': horizontal, whereas the crest is a vertical feature; the horizontal disjunct of this same sentence is already carried by `drv.road.curved_alignment`, whose contract states that a vertical curve, a grade or a crest is not denoted.

span: where such vehicle cannot be seen by the driver of any other vehicle approaching from either direction within 500 feet.
proposal: | `st.sight_distance` | the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other, from the eye of either driver to the body of the other vehicle at the height convention the source declares: both the view of approaching traffic from that point and its being seen by drivers approaching it, whether or not any road user is there **Not a stand-in for:** whether an actual road user saw, or could see, another at an observation (`rel.visible`), or the clarity of the air (`env.visibility`) | general |

rel.visible - 'b is visible from a: an unobstructed line of sight from a's reference point to b's body, as the source tests it': a relation between road users present at an observation, so it is unknown where no other vehicle is present, while the span asks whether the vehicle could be seen by any vehicle approaching, present or not

span: must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
proposal: A relation giving the side of a structure region with respect to a road user's direction of travel - whether a region (here the dividing space, barrier or section, or a roadway of the divided way) lies to the road user's right or to its left, as a side or a signed lateral offset in that road user's own frame. 'must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway' is, on a divided highway, the subject being upon a roadway with the dividing structure on its left; nothing in the closed set carries that. st.region_geometry gives only world-frame geometry and an unsigned ground distance, and rel.bearing, the one atom that gives a direction in a road user's own frame, ranges over road users and not over regions. The planned reading of this span - the concept drv.motion.travel_opposes_lane_direction, the right-hand roadway taken as the roadway whose lanes are designated for the way the subject travels - is what the behaviour review struck down in both directions, and it is not a narrowing this record may adopt: it calls lawful conduct unlawful as well as the reverse. No other mapping of these words is available over this vocabulary, and the span is the whole obligation of the node, so nothing of it can be carried as a residue. The operator may give the element as an atom of the rel family (the direction, or the signed lateral position, of a structure region from a road user in that road user's frame - the counterpart of rel.bearing for regions, which a source supplies measured as it supplies rel.bearing), or equivalently as a Core primitive over st.region_geometry, kin.position and kin.heading returning the signed lateral offset of a region from a road user's path, the formula language writing no geometric computation of a side. Either would also let a concept for the roadways of a divided way - which one of them a road user is upon - be defined once and called by id, rather than rebuilt in a rule.
nearest: rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of", "immediately to the rear")' - the family is relations between road users and b is a road user, so it gives no direction of a structure region such as a dividing section or a roadway

st.region_geometry: 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame, and the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)' - the distance is unsigned and the geometry world-frame, so which side of the dividing structure the road user is on is not read from it; its own exclusion is occupancy, not side

drv.road.divided_way: 'Not a stand-in for: which roadway of the divided way the road user is upon, or which side of the dividing structure it is on, neither of which this reports' - the concept that carries s2 expressly refuses the element s3 needs

drv.motion.travel_opposes_lane_direction: 'Not a stand-in for: ... which half of the roadway the road user is on, which the caller reads' - and the caller cannot read it here: the review found a vehicle on the left-hand roadway travelling with its lanes' designation violated by the law and compliant under this concept, and a vehicle on the right-hand roadway travelling against its lane's designation compliant under the law and violated under it

st.lane_adjacency: 'left / right neighbouring lane of the same direction; lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction' - it orders lanes within one carriageway and says nothing of which carriageway of a divided way lies to the road user's right

st.roadway: 'the part of a highway improved for vehicular traffic, excluding shoulder; separate roadways of a divided highway are separate' - the kind atom tells the two roadways apart but does not say which of them is the right-hand one for a road user's direction of travel

proposal: Nothing waits for this record and nothing the vocabulary can carry is left in it. (1) No user: the one node listed, NRS_484B_223_1b, does not claim the concept, so the record answers no clause element of this run. (2) The missing operator: the contract fixes the earlier end of its comparison at one instant - 'at the first observation of the window behind' - and makes the verdict unknown where occupancy is unobserved 'at either end of the window'. The formula language has no operator that evaluates a formula at the observation a window's length behind, and no Term that reads an atom there: holdsFor/within are 'at every observation in the window' behind and ahead, atLast m d s psi phi is phi at the last observation at which psi held (with psi = tt, the current one, and no instant-local psi marks a window's first observation, since which observation that is depends on where the window is anchored), since/once/always/eventually are unbounded, rises reaches exactly one observation back, and Term.sinceRise, Term.count and Term.distanceWhile report the start or the extent of a run, not a value at a chosen instant. The gap is an operator gap: a past-instant reading, e.g. atFirst m d s phi, phi at the first observation of the window of length d behind, unknown (windowTruncated) where that window reaches past the start of the trace. (3) No split carries the notion: the words are one notion, a departure from one lane over one window, not two the vocabulary holds apart, and neither side of any split escapes the same two-instant comparison. (4) The expressible remainder is already accepted: the nearest reading the language writes - the footprint overlaps at the observation no lane it overlapped in the window behind - is the accepted concept drv.lane.moved_out_of_lane, over the same sort (user : track), the same parameter (window, s) and the same atoms (rel.occupies, st.lane, kin.time); it differs from this record only in taking the past overlap existentially over the window rather than at the window's first observation, which is precisely the distinction no operator can draw. A node that needs these words calls drv.lane.moved_out_of_lane and declares on its own span how the window's earlier end is read, or waits for the operator above.

Two things the vocabulary does not carry, both needed before the third limb of the cascade can be written at all. First, a relation naming the ways that form an intersection - which highways or roadways meet there - so that the way crossing a road user's own approach can be told from the way it came by and from any other way of the scene; the ontology ties a lane to the intersection it runs into (`st.lane_enters`) and says nothing of the way that lane lies on, so 'the intersecting highway' cannot be named at all. Second, and not supplied by the first, a sight distance read from a road user's place along another way - the length of the crossing way that can be seen from where the road user stands, the intersection sight triangle the words 'a view of approaching traffic on the intersecting highway' state. `st.sight_distance` is read of one region and is the view along the road a vehicle on it is upon; read of the highway the subject itself stands on it answers a different question, which is what the behaviour review found in both directions (a halt made well back where the subject's own way has the sight distance, with no view of the crossing way, read as compliant; a halt made at the forward-most point from which the crossing way can be seen read as violated). s5 is a condition span and s6 is the standard it governs: the standard cannot be bounded without the view of that way, and a rule that reads the subject's own way in its place approximates the span with a neighbouring atom rather than carrying it. With these two atoms the span is writable: the highway that meets the intersection the subject's approach lane runs into, and the sight distance along it from the subject's stopping place, held against `p.view_sight_distance`.
nearest: st.sight_distance: 'the distance along the road within which a vehicle at a point and another vehicle on the road could see each other, from the eye of either driver to the body of the other vehicle at the height convention the source declares' - it is read of one region, so it carries the view along the road the road user is upon and no view from a place on one way onto another way; it is also 'not a stand-in for whether an actual road user saw, or could see, another at an observation (`rel.visible`)', which leaves the law's view of a way that need not carry any traffic unexpressed

Not a stand-in for ... the sight distance of a place (`st.sight_distance`) - what could be seen from or at a place, whether or not any road user is there, is that atom' - it needs an actual road user to be there, and the law asks of approaching traffic that need not be in the scene

proposal: A relation over this vocabulary that can carry "shall not follow another vehicle" on any scene. The catalogued concept `drv.interaction.following` denotes exactly this span, but as built it is decided false for every pair of road users: its alignment conjunct hands the formal parameter `following_alignment_tolerance`, declared by the concept and catalogued in the reading (`p.following_alignment_tolerance`) in degrees, straight to `rel.same_direction`, whose tolerance is a cosine; a cosine never exceeds 1 while a degree figure for an admissible misalignment does, so "the two headings are aligned within the alignment tolerance the caller sets" is false for perfectly aligned headings, and it is false alike under the other order of the concept's two formals, the reach being larger still. The coding session showed this on four distinct geometries - two identical cars in one and the same lane 10 m apart with identical headings, the bodies staggered laterally inside the lane so that both components of the surface gap are positive, occupancy derived from the polygons and then stated outright, and the subject leading instead of trailing - the result decided `compliant` in every one, never `unknown`, so no atom the concept reads is merely absent from the scenes; the order, the lane and the gap conjuncts are each eliminated by one of those runs. What is missing is a following relation whose alignment is expressible: either a cosine-valued alignment formal on that concept, with its catalogue unit and the reading parameter corrected to a ratio, or a conversion from degrees to a cosine inside the concept's own body. The formula language has no trigonometry, so neither a rule nor a concept body can convert the one into the other as the pair (concept, reading) now stands, and the repair lies in the concept's file and the reading's catalogue, in neither of which this record can reach. Until it is made, every rule of this law is vacuous: the duty can never be engaged against a vehicle being followed, which is why the `forbid` and the four `branch_<n>` witnesses that fix the bound report compliance. The record's other spans need nothing: s1, s3 and s4 map as planned, the standard on s3 is bounded by the time-headway convention with a closing allowance and a density increment, and the gate refused only the witnesses whose verdict turns on s2.
nearest: drv.interaction.following: "both footprints overlap one and the same lane, l's body lies ahead of f's along that lane's direction, the two headings are aligned within the alignment tolerance the caller sets, and the longitudinal distance between the two bodies is at most the reach the caller sets" - the contract denotes the span whole, and the node maps s2 to it for that reason, but the third conjunct as built admits no pair of headings whatever, so the concept carries the span in its words and on no scene.

rel.same_direction: "headings aligned within a tolerance" - the atom the concept calls, and the place the degree figure is consumed as a cosine; the parameter catalogue holds no cosine-valued alignment tolerance to pass it, `p.following_alignment_tolerance` being deg. It could not stand in for the span in any case: the ontology's §9 makes "a following gap" a concept node, "called by id" and "never rebuilt inline" from its atoms, and the termination rule's clause 3 says the same.

rel.ahead_behind_in_lane: "a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction" - carries the order along the lane alone, neither the reach within which a leading vehicle is the one followed nor the alignment of the two headings, so it is not "follow"; and it is one of the atoms of the concept the ontology forbids rebuilding inline.

rel.centre_distance: "Not a stand-in for: a clearance between bodies or an order of arrival" - a proximity decides neither who travels behind whom nor the space kept between the bodies, so it cannot carry "follow another vehicle" nor the standard on s3 that measures what that following owes.

span: shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
proposal: An atom for how distinctly the transverse marking of a stop line is painted, as a road user approaching it would see it - a clarity in {clear, faded, obliterated}: a marking that stands out distinctly on the surface, one whose paint is worn but still discernible, and one no longer discernible. The whole cascade of c4 turns on it: only a clearly marked stop line is the place of the halt, and a line whose marking is not clear is 'none' for these words, so that the duty falls through to the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection and, failing that, to the point nearest the intersection where the view of approaching traffic is afforded. With no contract that distinguishes clarity, every stop line the source carries is read as clearly marked: the rule then demands the halt at a worn or obliterated line where the law requires it before the crossing, and withholds the crossing limb where the law grants it - the difference changes what the law requires, in both directions, which is the structural finding upheld against this record at iterations 4 and 5. The want cannot be repaired by re-reading the words or by another atom: the distinctness of a painted marking is a physical property of the road surface, not a legal status presumed from the feature's presence (the line's presence is evidence that a line was laid down, never that its paint is still distinct), not an intention, perception or purpose read through conduct, and not a category a jurisdiction declares administratively. Carrying the span by st.stop_line alone is an approximation by a broader contract, so the record is withdrawn rather than bent to it.
nearest: st.stop_line: 'the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device' - the contract carries only the presence of a transverse halt marking and the device it serves; it admits a marking in any condition and says nothing of how distinctly it is painted, so a worn or obliterated line is a stop line under it and the word 'clearly' excludes nothing

st.crosswalk: 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection; marked attribute' - the marked attribute tells a crossing that carries a marking from the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks, which is whether a marking was laid down and not how distinctly it is painted; and it is an attribute of a crossing, never of a stop line

st.lane_marking: 'per side of a lane: type in {none, broken, solid, double_solid, solid_broken, dotted, curb}, colour in {white, yellow, other}' - type and colour give the pattern and the hue of the marking of a lane's side, never its distinctness, and the atom is of a lane's longitudinal side, not of the transverse line where vehicles halt

st.region_geometry: 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame, and the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it' - it carries where a stop line region lies and how far the subject's body stands from it, and nothing whatever about the condition of the paint that marks it
